title: The statutory electronic-prescription mandate and the exceptions the commissioner establishes by regulation
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 17(a) no controlled substance in Schedule II may be dispensed without an electronic prescription from a practitioner, except that under s. 17(b), IN EMERGENCY SITUATIONS, AS DEFINED BY THE COMMISSIONER, a schedule II, III, IV, V or VI substance may be dispensed upon written prescription or oral prescription IN ACCORDANCE WITH SECTION 20 AND RELATED REGULATIONS; under s. 17(c) a controlled substance included in Schedule III, IV, V or VI shall not be dispensed without an electronic prescription from a practitioner. Under s. 23(g) prescribers shall issue an electronic prescription for all controlled substances and medical devices, and the department shall promulgate regulations setting forth standards for electronic prescriptions. Under s. 23(h) THE COMMISSIONER, THROUGH REGULATION, SHALL ESTABLISH EXCEPTIONS to section 17 and subsection (g) authorizing the limited use of a written and oral prescription where appropriate, and the exceptions SHALL BE LIMITED TO: (i) prescriptions issued by veterinarians; (ii) prescriptions issued or dispensed in circumstances where electronic prescribing is not available due to temporary technological or electrical failure; (iii) a time-limited waiver process for practitioners who demonstrate economic hardship, technological limitations that are not reasonably within the control of the practitioner, or other exceptional circumstance; (iv) prescriptions that are issued or dispensed in emergency situations as defined by the commissioner pursuant to said section 17, including situations where the electronic prescription requirement would result in a delay that would adversely impact the patient's medical condition; (v) when a prescription cannot be issued electronically under federal or state law or regulations; (vi) prescriptions issued outside the jurisdiction of the commonwealth; and (vii) other exceptions to said section 17 and said subsection (g) as the commissioner determines necessary, provided that 90 days before promulgating or amending any regulations regarding other exceptions the commissioner files a written report setting forth the justification with the house and senate committees on ways and means, the joint committee on public health, and the joint committee on mental health, substance use and recovery.
exam_relevance: Tests the statutory frame behind every Massachusetts ePrescribing exception: the mandate is statutory, each exception exists as one the commissioner establishes through regulation under s. 23(h), and s. 17(b) sends an emergency written or oral prescription to section 20 and the related regulations.

authority.name: Necessity of prescription for dispensing controlled substances
Electronic prescription requirement and the commissioner's exceptions

exceptions: Section 17(b) permits written or oral dispensing of a schedule II through VI substance in emergency situations as defined by the commissioner, in accordance with section 20 and related regulations.
The s. 23(h) exceptions take effect as the commissioner establishes them through regulation rather than directly from the statute.
common_confusions: Reading s. 17(a) or s. 17(c) as an unqualified bar on non-electronic dispensing, when s. 17(b) and the s. 23(h) exceptions qualify them.

Treating the s. 23(h) list as open-ended, when the statute says the exceptions shall be limited to the listed categories, the last of which is other exceptions the commissioner determines necessary after the required advance report.
Assuming every s. 23(h) exception is applied for; only the time-limited waiver process is described that way in the statute.
verification_notes: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 17 and s. 23(g) and (h) read in the current text on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
